Please solve this issue: The support console gets a single entry point for refunds. Add `process_refund_request(payment, amount, requested_by, at)` in a new module `ledgerly/support.py`. `amount` is the text the support agent typed (for example "49.99"; amounts with more than two decimals are rounded to the cent), `requested_by` is the agent's user id and `at` is when the request was made. Only captured payments can be refunded, the amount must be positive, and the total refunded must never exceed the captured amount. Apply the refund to the payment (keep the running total in `payment.refunded_amount`; set `payment.status` to `"refunded"` once the full amount has been refunded) and return the payment.

## Notes from earlier work
These notes were distilled from earlier work in this repository that passed verification. Follow them unless the code or CHANGELOG.md shows they no longer hold.
- [at-c0076] Support refund request detail: Keep support refund request functions short; move parsing into a private _parse helper in the same module.
  (learned from task T4076 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-c0080] Support refund request detail: The support refund request report pads values to 50 characters so the columns line up.
  (learned from task T4080 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-c0071] Payment detail: Support asked for payment reasons as free text of at most 120 characters.
  (learned from task T4071 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0009] Record audit entry for every balance change: Every operation that moves money or changes a payment, credit or invoice balance must call ledgerly.audit.record("<past_tense_event>", <entity>_id=..., amount=...) with payment_id=... or invoice_id=...; finance reconciles the ledger from these entries.
  (learned from task E06 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0006] Money-moving functions take idempotency_key: Every function that moves money or changes a payment, credit or invoice balance (e.g. refund in ledgerly/adjustments.py) must accept keyword-only idempotency_key=None, check ledgerly.audit.events() for an existing entry with that key first and return the original record without reapplying, and include idempotency_key in the audit.record call.
  (learned from task E04 on ledgerly 1.0.0; source INC-204; relied on 1x, 0 passed, 1 failed)
  WARNING: a recent task that relied on this note failed a related review check.
- [at-0008] Normalize money and timestamps at entry: Normalize inputs at the top of money-handling functions: use ledgerly.money.round_money and ZERO for amounts and ledgerly.clock.ensure_utc for timestamps, and raise ledgerly.errors.BillingError with a snake_case code for validation failures.
  (learned from task E04 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)

## Code review of your previous attempt
Your previous attempt at this issue was reviewed and not accepted. The repository still contains that attempt. Address every comment below:
- [team convention] Every operation that moves money or changes a payment, credit or invoice balance must accept an optional keyword-only `idempotency_key=None` (callers without a key keep working). Check the key first, before validating state: if an audit entry with the same key already exists (ledgerly.audit.events()), return the original result (for functions that return a record, the same record) without applying the operation again. Include `idempotency_key` in the audit entry you write. Introduced after the double-refund incident INC-204.
- [team convention] Support-initiated refunds and credits above 500.00 need a second approver (finance policy FIN-2026-03): accept an optional keyword-only `approved_by=None` (callers that do not need approval keep working). Amounts at or below 500.00 need no approval; above it, raise BillingError("approval_required") when `approved_by` is missing.
